Senses.Explanation: In Chan records this is a recurrent further-up register, especially in compounds translated as “the upward matter,” “the one road upward,” “the upward vehicle of the house,” “the upward barrier” or “upward barrier-latch,” “an upward move,” “the upward aperture,” “the upward pivot,” “an upward person,” “the upward handle,” and “the upward pincers and hammer.” It is explicitly contrasted with “downward.” Records quote, “The one road upward, the thousand sages do not transmit,” and ask what the untransmitted upward matter is. Another recurrent question asks whether there is still an upward matter; in one recorded case the answer is “no.” Records also ask directly, “What is the upward vehicle of the house?” The expression identifies this upward or further-up register but is not given a single explanatory gloss by the records.
Senses.Note: This is the primary corpus-wide sense and is distinct from ordinary spatial direction. It appears in a family of compounds and questions and is explicitly paired with “downward.” Each occurrence is attributed to the identified person who deploys or records it. Compare “the one road upward,” “downward,” “the upward matter,” and “the upward vehicle of the house.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問向上一路千聖不傳如何是向上不傳底事
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lamp Highlights Collection (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), Renwang Jun section: a monk asks Renwang Jun about the untransmitted matter of the one road upward. Renwang Jun is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正當一色時還有向上事也無
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), Qinglin Shiqian section: Qinglin Shiqian raises Caoshan Benji's exchange in which Guibian asks whether an upward matter remains and Caoshan answers no. Qinglin Shiqian is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧便問如何是向上宗乘
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Sayings Record (古尊宿語錄), Yunmen Wenyan section: after Yunmen Wenyan rejects other acts as the upward vehicle of the house, a monk asks what that vehicle is.

Occurrences.Kwic: 向上關捩子有此眼目方辨得邪正宗黨
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Sayings Record (古尊宿語錄), Huangbo Xiyun section: Huangbo Xiyun places the upward barrier-latch beside the eye that distinguishes true and false lineages.

Occurrences.Kwic: 處處盡歌皇化，何須演妙譚元。向上一竅又且如何？驀拈拄杖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Jingguang Weijue section: Jingguang Weijue asks about the further-up aperture, then lifts and strikes down his staff. Jingguang Weijue is not yet in the roster.

Senses.Explanation: The ordinary locational sense is “up” or “upward,” distinct from the recurrent register in the first sense. It appears in phrases such as “look upward,” “eyebrows raised upward,” “head upward,” and “above is.” One passage says, “Raise the eyebrows and look up: above, no sky is seen; look down: below, no ground is seen.” The attachment to looking, the eyebrows, or the head and the direct pairing with downward movement identify the spatial sense.
Senses.Note: This secondary corpus-wide sense prevents every occurrence from being forced into the recurrent upward register. It is independently attested across multiple files.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眉毛向上看，上不見天。向下看，下不見地。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Seven Assemblies Record of Muyun Tongmen (牧雲和尚七會語錄): Muyun Tongmen uses the spatial sense in paired directions, looking upward and downward. Muyun Tongmen is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 向上看佗師口恰似失妳孩兒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lamp Highlights Collection (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), Baozhi praise section: Baozhi uses looking upward in a simile. Baozhi is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 剔起眉毛向上看，丈夫自有沖天憤。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sayings Record of Tianyin Yuanxiu (天隱和尚語錄): Tianyin Yuanxiu's verse instructs the listener to raise the eyebrows and look upward.
